2027-06-04.title: Friday of the second week after Pentecost · Memory of Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos
readings: Remember your leaders; Jesus suffered outside the city gate; we have an altar
The faithful and wise slave whom the master finds at work
The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep
“I am the way, and the truth, and the life”
“No one has greater love than this”
2027-06-04.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Second Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam keeps today the memory of Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos (2019), with the readings for the memory of a bishop and three alternative Gospels; these are the only readings printed for the day. It also notes that the Latin Church celebrates today the solemnity of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus. First Friday of the month (Panchangam 2026–27, p. 56).
2027-06-04.verse: Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the city gate in order to sanctify the people by his own blood. Let us then go to him outside the camp and bear the abuse he endured.
theo: Three remembrances meet on this first Friday of June. The Panchangam asks us to remember Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos, a bishop of our Church who went to the Lord in 2019. It notes that the Latin Church celebrates today the solemnity of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, and June has long been kept by Catholics of every rite in Kerala as the month of the Sacred Heart. And it is the First Friday, when many of our families go to confession and receive Holy Communion in reparation and love. The readings chosen for the memory of a bishop gather all three together. The Letter to the Hebrews begins: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.” We remember a bishop not only with gratitude for what he did, but with a prayer that the Lord who called him may receive him, and with a resolve to imitate what was Christlike in him. The memory of a shepherd always sends us back to the Shepherd whose heart was the source of his.

The letter then says something remarkable: “We have an altar from which those who officiate in the tent have no right to eat.” The Christian altar is not a table of ordinary food; it is the place where the one sacrifice of Christ is made present. And where was that sacrifice offered? “Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the city gate in order to sanctify the people by his own blood. Let us then go to him outside the camp and bear the abuse he endured.” Outside the gate, on the hill of Calvary, one of the soldiers opened his side with a spear, and blood and water flowed out. That pierced side is what the Church contemplates in the devotion to the Sacred Heart: not a sentimental picture but the wound through which we see the love of God made flesh. St Bonaventure wrote that his side was pierced so that, through the visible wound, we might see the invisible wound of love (The Tree of Life, in substance). Hebrews draws the practical conclusion: “Through him, then, let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name. Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.” Praise and sharing: this is how a heart that has been loved answers.

The Gospel shows the same love in the shape of a steward's faithfulness: “Who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give the other slaves their allowance of food at the proper time? Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives.” A bishop is such a steward; so is a priest, a parent, a teacher, a nurse on night duty. The wicked servant thinks “My master is delayed” and begins to treat others as he pleases. The faithful one keeps feeding the household, because he knows whose household it is. The alternative Gospels printed today show the heart of the Master who appoints the stewards: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.” “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.” “No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends.” On this First Friday, let us thank God for the shepherds who fed us with his word and his Body, pray for the soul of Mar Timotheos, and bring our own hearts to the pierced Heart of Christ, so that they may become a little more like his: gentle, humble, faithful, and ready to share.
outline: Ask: whose faith have I received, and whose faith am I handing on?
A bishop's memory sends us back to the Shepherd's heart.
The pierced side, the altar, and the sacrifice of praise and sharing.
Feeding the household on time, because it is the Master's household.
“Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
live: Pray today for the bishop who confirmed you or the priest who baptized you, living or departed, and for the soul of Mar Timotheos.
Keep this First Friday by sharing something you have with someone in need, as an offering of love to the Heart of Jesus.
2027-06-04.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, good shepherd, whose side was pierced outside the city gate so that blood and water might flow for the life of the world, we remember today your servant, Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos, whom you called to shepherd your people. Grant him rest and light in your presence. On this First Friday we bring our hearts to your Heart: make them gentle and humble like yours, faithful in the tasks you have given us, and generous in praise and in sharing. Give your Church shepherds after your own heart. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: “We have an altar.” Every Holy Qurbono stands at the foot of the Cross outside the city gate: the Body given and the Blood poured out from the pierced side are offered and received. The First Friday Communion is a return of love to the Heart that loved first.
conn: Hebrews 13:7–16 and Matthew 24:45–51 are the readings the Panchangam gives for the memory of a bishop; the alternative Gospels (John 10, 14 and 15) show the heart of the Good Shepherd.
A heart pierced outside the gate.
Hebrews 13:12 speaks of Jesus suffering outside the city gate; John 19:34 tells of the soldier who pierced his side there. The Latin solemnity of the Sacred Heart today reads John 19:31–37.
fathers: His side was pierced by the spear so that through the visible wound we might see the invisible wound of love, and enter into his heart (The Tree of Life, in substance).

From his side came water and blood, the symbols of Baptism and of the holy mysteries: from these the Church is born, as Eve was formed from the side of the sleeping Adam (Baptismal Catecheses 3, in substance).
magis: Jesus knew and loved us each and all during his life, his agony and his Passion, and gave himself up for each one of us. He has loved us all with a human heart; for this reason the Sacred Heart of Jesus, pierced by our sins and for our salvation, is rightly considered the chief sign and symbol of that love.

In his encyclical on the human and divine love of the Heart of Jesus, Pope Francis invites the Church to rediscover in the pierced Heart of Christ the source of her mission and of a love that reaches out to the wounded world.

quick: The Panchangam remembers Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos (2019) with the readings for a bishop's memory; it is also the First Friday, and the Latin Church keeps the solemnity of the Sacred Heart.
Hebrews: remember your leaders and imitate their faith; Jesus suffered outside the city gate; we have an altar; offer the sacrifice of praise and share what you have.
The faithful and wise servant feeds the household at the proper time and is found at work when the master comes.
2027-06-04.action: Make a First Friday act of love today: confession, Communion, or a visit to the Blessed Sacrament, and one gift to someone in need.
2027-06-04.question: Am I a faithful steward of what the Lord has put in my charge, or do I tell myself that the Master is delayed?

family.explain: Today we remember a bishop, Geevarghese Mar Timotheos, who went to heaven in 2019. A bishop is a shepherd for God's people. Jesus is the Good Shepherd: he loves his sheep so much that he gave his life for them. On the Cross a soldier opened Jesus' side and blood and water came out. Many Christians remember that open Heart on the First Friday of the month. It tells us how much Jesus loves each one of us.
family.intention: We pray for our bishops and priests, and for Mar Timotheos, that he may rest with the Good Shepherd.
family.ask: Ask: “Who are the shepherds who have taken care of my faith, and how can I thank them?”

illus: In a parish near Thiruvalla, an old sacristan kept a small notebook in the drawer beside the vestments. Over forty years he had written in it the names of the bishops who had come to the parish for confirmations, ordinations and feasts, with the date and one sentence about each visit. One line said only: he stayed after the Qurbono to bless every sick person in the parish, house by house, in the rain. When a young priest asked him why he wrote such things down, the old man said: the Letter to the Hebrews says remember your leaders; I am an old man and I forget, so I write. Then he added: I write down the good they did so that I can copy it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, good shepherd, gentle and humble of heart, we gather at your pierced side on this First Friday. Teach us to love as you love. Amen.
share: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). Which shepherd's faith do I most want to imitate?
Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the city gate in order to sanctify the people by his own blood (Hebrews 13:12). What does the pierced Heart of Jesus say to me today?
Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives (Matthew 24:46). What work has the Lord put in my hands?
pm.resp: Heart of Jesus, make our hearts like yours.
interc: For the soul of Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos, and for all the departed bishops of our Church, that they may rest in the peace of the Good Shepherd.
For our Major Archbishop, our bishops and priests, that they may be shepherds after the heart of Christ.
For all who keep the First Friday, that their love for the Heart of Jesus may bear fruit in mercy and sharing.
For all who are hurt, lonely or tired of life, that they may find rest in the gentle and humble Heart of Jesus.
For parents, teachers and all who are stewards in God's household, that they may be found faithful at work when the Lord comes.
pm.close: Father, from the pierced side of your Son flowed blood and water, the fountain of the Church's life. Give rest to your servant Mar Timotheos, give your Church faithful shepherds, and make our hearts like the Heart of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: The custom of receiving Holy Communion on the first Friday of each month in honour of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, often with confession beforehand, as an act of love and reparation. It spread from the seventeenth century through the devotion associated with St Margaret Mary Alacoque, and many Catholic families in Kerala, in every rite, keep it faithfully.

homily: Dear friends, today the Panchangam asks us to remember Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos, a bishop of our Church who went to the Lord in 2019. It is also the First Friday, and the Latin Church celebrates today the Sacred Heart of Jesus. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7).

Then it says: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:8). Bishops and priests come and go; the Lord who sends them remains. And Hebrews shows us where his love was poured out: Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the city gate in order to sanctify the people by his own blood (Hebrews 13:12). There, on Calvary, a soldier pierced his side, and blood and water came out. That open Heart is the source of every shepherd's love.

The Gospel asks: Who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household? (Matthew 24:45). A bishop is such a servant, but so is every father and mother, every teacher, every one of us who has someone to care for. Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives (Matthew 24:46).

So today let us pray for the soul of Mar Timotheos and for all our shepherds. Let us bring our hearts to the Heart of Jesus in confession and Communion on this First Friday. And let us do what Hebrews asks: offer a sacrifice of praise, and do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God (Hebrews 13:16). Amen.
kids: Children, today we remember a bishop called Mar Timotheos, who has gone to be with Jesus. A bishop is like a shepherd who looks after God's people. But the best shepherd of all is Jesus. Jesus loves us so much that he gave his life for us on the Cross. Today is the First Friday, when many people remember the Heart of Jesus, full of love for us. You can give Jesus a gift from your heart today: share something with a friend, or say thank you to Jesus for loving you.

intro: Theme: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”

On Friday of the second week after Pentecost, the memory of Most Rev. Geevarghese Mar Timotheos, the First Friday, and the day the Latin Church keeps the Sacred Heart: remembering our shepherds, the Heart pierced outside the gate, and the faithful steward.

sub: Those who spoke the word of God to us.
Consider the outcome; imitate the faith.
q: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.
And when the chief shepherd appears, you will win the crown of glory that never fades away.
points.apply: Write down this week the name of one bishop, priest or catechist who gave you the faith, and one thing in them you want to imitate.

points.h: Outside the gate: the pierced Heart
sub: Jesus suffered outside the city gate.
Blood and water from the opened side.
We have an altar: praise and sharing.
q: so that, when they look on the one whom they have pierced, they shall mourn for him
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
points.apply: Keep the First Friday this month and the next with confession, Communion and one act of sharing.

sub: Put in charge of the household.
Found at work when the master comes.
q: The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.
Moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.
points.apply: Name the people the Lord has put in your care, and do one faithful, unnoticed act of care for each this week.

concl: We remember our shepherds and pray for them, and their memory sends us to the Heart of the Good Shepherd, pierced outside the gate.
From that Heart comes the strength to be faithful stewards in the household of God.
2027-06-04.resolve: Imitate the faith of your shepherds, bring your heart to the Heart of Jesus, and be found faithful at work.
